module.purpose: Defines the React context, provider, and hooks used to coordinate SVG export behavior in the editor.
module.summary: This module establishes the public contract for SVG export consumers, including export definition registration, deferred export completion, asset URL resolution, color mode, scaling, and pixel ratio. It provides a React context provider that wires export state into editor and container providers, plus hooks for accessing the context and delaying export until asynchronous shape data is ready.
module.businessContext: Supports tldraw document export to SVG and raster formats. Failures can produce incomplete exports, unresolved assets, or incorrect appearance and scaling.
classes: SvgExportDef (~L10-13): Describes deferred SVG definition content identified by a unique key.
SvgExportContext (~L16-50): Exposes export coordination, asset resolution, and rendering configuration.
functions: getElement (~L12-12): Produces optional SVG definition content synchronously or asynchronously.
addExportDef (~L18-20): Registers uniquely keyed content for the SVG definitions section.
waitUntil (~L28-28): Delays export completion until a supplied promise resolves.
resolveAssetUrl (~L34-34): Resolves an asset identifier for the requested export width.
SvgExportContextProvider (~L53-71): Supplies export context alongside editor and container providers.
useSvgExportContext (~L78-80): Returns the active SVG export context or null.
useDelaySvgExport (~L97-110): Creates a callback that releases a deferred SVG export.
systemCapabilities: Integrate export rendering with editor providers

typeShapes.name: SvgExportDef
SvgExportContext
typeShapes.shape:
{
	/**
	 * Add contents to the `<defs>` section of the export SVG. Each export def should have a unique
	 * key. If multiple defs come with the same key, only one will be added.
	 */
	addExportDef(def: SvgExportDef): void

	/**
	 * Cause the SVG export to be delayed until the returned promise is resolved. This is useful if
	 * e.g. your shape loads data dynamically, and you need to prevent the export from happening
	 * until after the data is loaded.
	 *
	 * See also the {@link useDelaySvgExport} hook, which may be a more convenient way to use this
	 * method depending on your use-case.
	 */
	waitUntil(promise: Promise<void>): void

	/**
	 * Resolve an asset URL in the context of this export. Supply the asset ID and the width in
	 * shape-pixels it'll be displayed at, and this will resolve the asset according to the export
	 * options.
	 */
	resolveAssetUrl(assetId: TLAssetId, width: number): Promise<string | null>

	/**
	 * Whether the export should be in dark mode.
	 */
	readonly isDarkMode: boolean

	/**
	 * The color mode to use for this export.
	 */
	readonly colorMode: 'light' | 'dark'

	/**
	 * The scale of the export - how much CSS pixels will be scaled up/down by.
	 */
	readonly scale: number

	/**
	 * Use this value to optionally downscale images in the export. If we're exporting directly to
	 * an SVG, this will usually be null, and you shouldn't downscale images. If the export is to a
	 * raster format like PNG, this will be the number of raster pixels in the resulting bitmap per
	 * CSS pixel in the resulting SVG.
	 */
	readonly pixelRatio: number | null
}

detail.name: SvgExportContextProvider
detail.signature: export function SvgExportContextProvider({ context, editor, children }: { context: SvgExportContext; editor: Editor; children: React.ReactNode })
preconditions: editor is a valid Editor instance.
postconditions: Descendant content is rendered within the supplied SVG export context.
The supplied editor is available to the provider's descendant content as required by the SVG export context.
invariants: The provided context value is preserved for descendants during the provider's render.
edgeCases: Any React children shape accepted by React.ReactNode is rendered as provider content.
The provider receives a non-null context because the context parameter is required.
detail.summary: Provides the SVG export context and editor to its descendant React content. Descendants can use the provider to access the supplied export configuration during rendering.

detail.name: useSvgExportContext
detail.summary: Provides access to the SVG export context for consumers of the editor's SVG export functionality.

units.name: useDelaySvgExport
units.source:
/**
 * Delay an SVG export until the returned function is called. This is useful if e.g. your shape
 * loads data dynamically, and you need to prevent the export from happening until after the data is
 * loaded.
 *
 * If used outside of an SVG export, this hook has no effect.
 *
 * @example
 * ```tsx
 * const readyForExport = useDelaySvgExport()
 *
 * return <MyDynamicComponent onDataLoaded={() => readyForExport()} />
 * ```
 *

detail.name: useDelaySvgExport
postconditions: When an SVG export is active, invoking the returned function permits the delayed export to continue.
invariants: Using the hook outside an SVG export does not produce an observable effect.
The hook does not itself trigger the delayed export before the returned function is invoked.
edgeCases: Called outside an SVG export: the returned function has no effect.
Invoked after dynamically loaded data is ready: the pending SVG export is allowed to proceed.
detail.summary: Returns a function that delays an SVG export until invoked, allowing dynamically loaded shape data to become ready first. When used outside an SVG export, the returned function has no effect.

specTests.when: The returned function is invoked after the data has loaded.
specTests.then: The delayed SVG export is allowed to proceed.
